items.title: Benny Waters interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995
items.q: But for all around entertaining and music combined, I think it was a better band than Count Basie.

ctx.x: Yeah. Ninety years, wow. Have you have occasion during your many years of experience, to work with either Count Basie or Joe Williams?

No I haven’t. No I haven’t. I wish I did. But I tell you I did work with a band that, well I may be saying something that people will agree, you know, but I had a pleasure working with Jimmie Lunceford and I thought it was a greater band than Count Basie. Not musically. Not musically. Exclusive musically. But for all around entertaining and music combined, I think it was a better band than Count Basie. So I had the pleasure of working with Jimmie a couple of years, I mean Jimmie Lunceford see. And I worked with…

items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: it's like Lockjaw and so forth left the Count Basie before Count Basie retired

ctx.x: Well, I could improvise, I always could improvise. I mean I knew harmony from, just from natural ability, I always could improvise. See, that's why I didn't like to - I was glad to be with this band because I had a chance to, more so than with my brother, all those dance bands. Dance band is commercial gig, you just play the music where it is and you get paid, but I mean, even big bands you don't - even big bands, that's, I'm sure of this, but I'm pretty sure a lot of these fine saxophonists, jazz men who left…

number had something there for tenor, see. But otherwise you don't get a chance to play. That's why Procope went back musically, I mean as far as choruses are concerned, on his horns. Procope was a great saxophone player then, on the period he was working with Kirby, you understand? But when he worked with these big bands playing first, he didn't get the chance, there was too many others.
